misconceptions.description: Disclosing AI use with a vague blanket statement that names no tool, location, or author edit
misconceptions.trigger: README says AI was used without specifying what, where, or how it was revised
misconceptions.feedback: Name the tool, the location (commit or section), and what you changed afterward. A blanket statement is not a usable disclosure.

misconceptions.description: Keeping the disclosure or traceability separate from the repository so a reader cannot check it against the code
misconceptions.trigger: design reasoning lives only in an external report, not alongside the code and assets
misconceptions.feedback: Co-locate the traceability matrix and disclosure in the repo so each screen change can be audited against the artifact.

misconceptions.description: Letting an AI write the disclosure of its own role, which it cannot truthfully report
misconceptions.trigger: learner accepts an AI-written account of what AI did in the project
misconceptions.feedback: Use AI only for the format. Supply the actual tools, commits, and edits yourself, since only you know what AI did here.

misconceptions.description: Making disclosure claims that cannot be checked because the commit history does not separate generated content from author edits
misconceptions.trigger: AI additions and author revisions are squashed or deleted from history
misconceptions.feedback: Keep AI-generated additions and your edits as separate commits so the disclosure can be verified against the diff.
